statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 futures have now held the same 29,535.25-29,594.25 band for a second hour since the 22:00 UTC restart, last 29,565.25 on roughly 3.8k contracts, so the weekend-gap risk that dominated the closed-venue hours has resolved without an adverse repricing and Tail eases further below the block threshold. Stress stays elevated on a restrictive Treasury curve, a stretched energy complex and an active Iran-US maritime conflict in which a prohibited zone has been signalled but not yet declared.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk remains concentrated in the narrow pre-Tokyo thin-liquidity window and, later, in the 22:00 UTC Tuesday restart, rather than across the whole outlook; every forecast hour maps below the block threshold. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures have held their 59-point reopen range into a second hour with no adverse weekend gap, while the signalled Iranian prohibited zone near Hormuz remains undeclared
body: The Sunday restart is now roughly ninety minutes old and the observed price path has not extended. NQ front-month last printed 29,565.25 inside an unchanged 29,535.25-29,594.25 session range on about 3.78k contracts, and ES traded 7,722.00 inside a 7,715.50-7,723.75 range on about 3.91k contracts. Volume has grown at a normal pace while the range has not, which is the signature of orderly two-way price discovery rather than directional efficiency. Against Friday's Nasdaq-100 cash close of 29,544.15 the restart remains effectively flat, so the adverse weekend gap that the closed-venue hours had carried as the principal conditional risk did not materialise and is now behind the assessment. Quoted change and percentage fields on both futures quotes remain unreliable at a Sunday restart, so the last price, the session range and the volume are treated as the observed evidence while the reopen change itself is not asserted. Tail is scored on that contained path. There is no shallow-pullback sequence, no repeated extension after a failed retracement, and no hold near a session extreme, which are the structures that define mean-reversion failure, so Tail falls from the prior hour and stays far below the block threshold. Cross-asset evidence supports the same reading. VIX last stood at 14.53 after a 13.80-14.58 Friday range, which is not a stressed equity-volatility regime. Delayed cross-asset context for the restart shows index futures within roughly a quarter of a percent of unchanged, gold flat and Treasury futures barely moved, with no safe-haven rotation under way. Latest-session internals were rotational rather than aligned: semiconductors were higher across the board, led by Micron, AMD, Arm and Intel, while five of eight Nasdaq megacaps fell, with Tesla and Apple the heaviest. That split argues against a one-way regime being carried into the new week. Stress nevertheless stays elevated, and the reasons are unchanged. The Federal Reserve H.15 release for September 3 shows the 2-year at 4.34%, the 10-year at 4.77% and the 30-year at 5.25%, a restrictive curve into a September 15-16 FOMC that sits outside this outlook window. The energy complex is stretched, with WTI near $92.11 and Brent near $96.78 after a roughly 9% weekly gain, and US diesel has been reported at a record $5.85 per gallon on the combination of Iran-related disruption and constrained refining. OPEC+ met on Sunday and left October quotas unchanged, pausing the unwinding of the 1.65 million barrel-per-day cut after six consecutive monthly increases, with the next meeting on October 4. The geopolitical picture remains a live two-way maritime conflict, and nothing has changed in the past hour. Following the verified weekend exchange in which the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at US warships and US forces struck three Iranian crude tankers, Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran will declare a prohibited zone beginning at the US Navy blockade line and extending toward Hormuz and into the Gulf, with any identified vessel placed on Iran's sanctions list. Verified reporting continues to confirm that the zone has been signalled but not yet declared, so it remains a conditional driver rather than observed evidence. It is also an incremental escalation rather than a new closure, because the Strait of Hormuz is already described as effectively closed with shipping traffic sharply reduced since fighting began on February 28, and the US blockade has already redirected 92 commercial vessels, which caps the marginal supply shock a declaration could deliver. Conditional risk in this outlook is therefore concentrated in the narrow window before Tokyo opens, where a headline discontinuity would meet the thinnest order book of the week, and that window still maps below the block threshold because gap risk without observed extension after a failed retracement is not evidence of mean-reversion failure. Monday September 7 is the US Labor Day holiday: US cash equity, ETF and listed options markets are closed for the full day, CME equity index futures trade a shortened session that halts at 17:00 UTC and restarts at 22:00 UTC for the Tuesday trade date, and the US data calendar is empty until Tuesday. The five closed hours from 17:00 to 21:00 UTC return Tail to the closed-venue floor by construction rather than by judgement. The next scheduled US items are the NFIB survey and the New York Fed consumer expectations release on Tuesday, ahead of PPI and Oracle results on September 10 and CPI on September 11, with reporting framing that inflation pair as the key input to the September policy debate.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Across the closed-venue hours Tail held a flat 5, with a single 4, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout, before stepping to 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart hour to carry reopen-gap risk. Stress climbed from 55 through a 52-60 band to a 60 high at 20:00 UTC as the Sunday geopolitical flow accumulated, then eased to 57 once the restart proved orderly. Confidence stayed in an 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal for every available hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the remainder of the Sunday restart, a full Asian and European session on the US Labor Day holiday, a shortened US futures session that halts at 17:00 UTC, five closed hours, and the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band for every hour, easing to 6 now that the reopen has proved contained, lifting to 8 around the Tokyo and European opens where a repricing would land without US cash depth, peaking at 9 in the final hour before the halt and again at the Tuesday restart, and sitting at the closed-venue floor of 5 while futures are halted. Stress starts at 56, holds in the low-to-mid 50s through the European and notional US hours, and unwinds toward 49 during the closed hours. Confidence decays from 86 to 64 across the window as live evidence gives way to conditional assumption. No US macro release falls inside the window; the next scheduled items are Tuesday's NFIB and New York Fed expectations releases, ahead of PPI on September 10 and CPI on September 11.
